Title: Crucial P510 test: Ahead of its time? - Basic Tutorials
URL: https://basic-tutorials.com/reviews/hardware-reviews/crucial-p510/
Published: 2025-05-15T15:00:50.000Z
Author: Niklas
Highlights:
With the Crucial P510, an extremely affordable PCI Express 5.0 SSD is coming onto the market that primarily addresses the issue of power consumption. In detail, this means a significantly more energy-efficient architecture, which should enable longer battery life and still offer the usual Gen5 transfer rates of up to 11,000 MB/s in sequential read and 9,500 MB/s in sequential write. In addition, the NVMe SSD is also backwards compatible and should therefore be ideal for gamers, creative minds and students in both the PC and notebook sector. The Crucial P510 is available in versions with 1 and 2 TB capacity and either with or without a heat sink. If you opt for the heatsink solution, you can expect a surcharge of currently around 12 euros.

If we go one level deeper, we notice that the Crucial P510 comes without DRAM. This is a pity, but in view of the low price of the SSD, it’s easy to get over. The P510 is powered by the Phison PS5031-E31T controller and Micron G9 276-layer 3D NAND is used for the NAND memory. However, there is no data encryption, only the Crucial Storage Executive is supplied by the manufacturer as an optional management tool. The PCIe Gen5x4 interface is available for data transfer, which provides read/write speeds of up to 11,000/9,500 MB/s for the SSD. The technical aspects are rounded off by adaptive thermal protection, TRIM and SMART support, adaptive garbage collection and ECC error code detection. Another advantage is the support of hibernation mode, which also reduces power consumption.

...

All the tests described below were carried out on this test system. The Crucial P510 1 TB was installed in the top M.2 slot of the motherboard, which natively supports PCIe 5.0 x4. The mainboard-specific M.2 heatsink was then installed. In this context, the following test results were determined as

...

The Crucial P510 1 TB can leave a good impression in the benchmarks and, thanks to PCIe 5.0, can be placed quite high up in the table. However, it turns out that even high-end PCIe 4.0 SSDs perform even better in individual tests. The powerful Phison controller does a decent job across the board and the performance values are consistent without thermal outliers.

If we now take a closer look at the AS SSD benchmark, it is noticeable that the Crucial P510 1TB is slightly below the manufacturer’s own T-series in terms of performance. While the Crucial T705 still delivers a massive lead, the P510 is most comparable with a slight gap to the T500. However, things are more uneven in the compression benchmark, which shows fluctuations in write performance even after several test attempts. With CrystalDiskMark, we achieve almost exactly the 11,000 MB/s specified by the manufacturer for sequential reads. When writing with the Crucial P510, we are slightly below the manufacturer’s specification of 9,500 MB/s with around 100 MB/s. In the 4K test, however, the P510, like its sister model Crucial P310, cannot quite shine and definitely loses performance. On the other hand, we landed in the upper midfield with access times of around 0.026. Here too, the Crucial P510 is almost on a par with the T-series, although not quite on a par.

...

After all these tests, the final question is whether the Crucial P510 is worth a recommendation. Basically, there are more ifs and buts here, because while the P510 hits the mark in terms of price compared to other PCIe 5.0 SSDs (currently 1 TB for around €100 or 2 TB for €190), you have to compromise on performance. One of the disadvantages is clearly the lack of DRAM cache, which also brings the manufacturer’s P310 to its knees to some extent. As a result, performance starts to slow down at times, especially when writing larger files. It is also regrettable that the P510 also has to make do without hardware-side encryption.

What does this mean overall? Basically, the Crucial P510 cuts a good figure all round and is particularly suitable for notebooks or PCs without a dedicated or ample heatsink. This makes it an affordable entry-level SSD in the PCIe 5.0 series, even if it cannot keep up with the company’s own T-series in terms of performance. So if you want to get the most out of your system, you should go for the Crucial T705. However, if you are looking for a balanced middle ground between performance and price, you can also consider the Crucial P510.

Product Overview

Crucial P510 CT1000P510SSD8 1TB PCIe Gen5 NVMe M.2 2280 SSD with read up to 11000 MB/s, write up to 9500 MB/s.

The Crucial P510 CT1000P510SSD8 is a 1TB internal solid state drive in M.2 2280 form factor. It utilizes PCIe Gen5 x4 NVMe interface, delivering sequential read speeds up to 11000 MB/s and sequential write speeds up to 9500 MB/s. Designed with G9 TLC NAND flash, it supports broad compatibility including laptops and desktops. Backward compatibility ensures operation with older PCIe generations. The drive features a black color design and is part of the Crucial P510 product line. As a dram-less SSD, it employs Host Memory Buffer for efficient performance. The Phison PS5031-E31T controller manages high-speed data transfers using Micron G9 276-layer 3D NAND storage memory. Available in 1TB and 2TB capacities, it suits mainstream performance needs in modern systems supporting PCIe 5.0.
